newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's oil minister to attend OPEC meeting - INA.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's oil minister to attend OPEC meeting - INA.

text.p: Iraq's Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed will attend OPEC meeting which will start in Vienna on Wednesday, the official Iraqi News Agency INA said on Sunday.

"General Amir Muhammad Rasheed explained that he would take part in OPEC's conference which will be held in the Austrian capital, Vienna, for the period between June 25 and 27," INA said in a dispatch from Amman where Rasheed was enroute to a visit to Spain.
It said the minister stressed that member states "should stick to the production ceiling of 25 million barrel per day set by the organisation."
Rasheed said Iraq would work for a stabilised price formula and securing "beneficial oil returns" for member states.
INA said Rasheed would also "brief the conference on the relations between Iraq and the (U.N.) Security Council."
The Council late on Saturday unanimously warned Iraq it would face further sanctions if it did not allow U.N. arms inspections.

Iraq's prevention of inspections of three sites this month prompted Rolf Ekeus, chairman of the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) in charge of dismantling Iraq's prohibited weapons, to complain to the council last week.
UNSCOM must certify Baghdad has no prohibited weapons before curbs on Iraq's oil exports are lifted. The U.N. sanctions were imposed for Baghdad's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The agency said Rasheed will also meet with the head of the Vienna-based International Atomic Energy Agency to discuss Iraq's past nuclear weapons programme.
